chunks: Logic gates from CMOS transistors. The question: Draw a NOT/AND/etc gate from transistors.
Inside a chip, logic gates are built from transistors, which act as tiny switches controlled by a voltage. A CMOS gate uses two teams of switches.
One team can connect the output to the supply voltage (a 1). The other can connect it to ground (a 0).
For any input, exactly one team is on, so the gate wastes almost no power when nothing is changing.
Imagine a bucket that holds the output level. A valve on a pipe from a high tank can fill it (a 1), and a valve on a drain can empty it (a 0).
The design rule is that the two are never both open and never both closed.
The CMOS inverter. The PMOS (top) connects Y to V DD when A is low; the NMOS (bottom) connects Y to ground when A is high.
Both gates share the input A and both drains share the output Y.
NMOS: a transistor switch that closes when its input is 1. It connects the output to ground. PMOS: a transistor switch that closes when its input is 0.
It connects the output to the supply. Supply and ground: the supply voltage is the "1" level, and ground (0 volts) is the "0" level.
In series / in parallel: switches in a line, where all must close to conduct, versus side by side, where any one is enough.
Inverter: one PMOS to the supply and one NMOS to ground, sharing the input. Input 0: the PMOS closes, the NMOS opens, so the output is 1. Input 1 reverses it, and the output is 0.
NAND: two NMOS in series to ground, two PMOS in parallel to the supply. With A = B = 1, both NMOS close, so the output is 0.
With A = 0 and B = 1, A's PMOS closes and the NMOS chain is broken, so the output is 1. That is the whole idea.
"The base cell is the CMOS inverter: a PMOS from VDD to the output, an NMOS from the output to ground, gates tied together.
Input low pulls the output up, input high pulls it down, and one is always off so there's no static current.
A NAND has two NMOS in series on the bottom and two PMOS in parallel on top; a NOR is the dual.
The rule is: pull-down implements the complement of the function, AND as series, OR as parallel, and the pull-up is the dual.
AND and OR are those gates plus an inverter, six transistors."
